note: Which keys of a translations.json are metadata, which are lines, which are neither. Until 2026-10-09 every product said 'a key starting with an underscore is metadata', and a game text beginning with one — a signature line drawn with underscores, a label found in a published translation — was skipped by every reader: the mod sent it to the model again at every launch, the site never counted, showed or published it. Metadata is now the closed list of names in spec/translation-file/schema.json; another underscore name is a line when its value has the shape of one, and left alone otherwise — the tolerance an older reader owes a newer writer's metadata.

is_metadata_key.out: bool: one of the names the tools write about a file

in.line_shaped: bool: the value is a JSON object with a 'v' member

is_line.out: bool: a line of the game's text

cases.why: a name of the contract is metadata — the properties of spec/translation-file/schema.json
the settings sections are metadata too
a key the game showed is not metadata
an underscore inside a key says nothing
a game's text can begin with an underscore — found in a published translation
the list is CLOSED: a name the contract does not hold is not metadata — a new one enters the schema and the list together
names are compared exactly, as JSON compares them
an empty key is not metadata
a key the game showed is a line
a name without a leading underscore is a line whatever its value — a reader still takes the bare string of the first format
a metadata name is never a line, even holding a {v} — a forged one must not reach the lineage
an underscore name holding a {v, t} is a line of the game: it is counted, shown, hashed and published like any other
a signature line drawn with underscores — read as metadata, it went to the model again at every launch
an underscore name the contract does not know, holding anything but a line, is a NEWER writer's metadata: left alone, neither a section nor an empty line
an empty key stays what it always was: a line (nothing writes one)
